eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from official sources and models centers on a high of 13–14°C for Buenos Aires on August 22, 2026, under clear to partly cloudy skies with light westerly winds and no precipitation.** The Argentine National Meteorological Service (SMN) explicitly forecasts a maximum of 14°C, aligning with multiple international models (Met Office, Yr.no) showing afternoon peaks near 13°C and US-based guidance (WeatherBug, WindBorne) converting 55°F highs to the same range.

Winter conditions in the Southern Hemisphere keep baseline August highs near 16–18°C on average, but a stable high-pressure pattern with dry air and modest insolation has suppressed warming today. Light winds (generally 4–7 m/s from the west or southwest) limit mixing and advection of warmer air, while dew points near or below 0°C further cap the daily maximum. Recent observations from the prior 24–48 hours show consistent cool mornings (lows 3–6°C) transitioning to modest afternoon recovery without exceeding model guidance.

Traders have priced 14°C as the clear mode (67.5% implied probability) because it matches the latest official forecast and ensemble consensus, with smaller probabilities on 13°C and 15°C reflecting minor model spread or measurement uncertainty at the observation site. No significant synoptic changes or forecast revisions have occurred to shift the distribution.
